WPMS No. 1372 of 2023
Hon’ble Ravindra Maithani, J.
Mr. M.C. Pant, Advocate for the 
petitioners.
Mr. Yogesh Pandey, Additional C.S.C. 
for the State.
Mr. Pankaj Raturi and Mr. D.C.S. 
Rawat, Advocates for the respondent no.3.
Heard. 
In fact, the Court had dictated the 
judgment in the open Court, but when the 
Court inquired, learned counsel for parties 
are agreeable that perhaps this matter may 
be decided by way of mediations.
It is a dispute with regard to the 
school, which was established by the father 
of the petitioner and the respondent no.3 
namely, Hansram Maithani. He constituted 
a society which was registered. The 
byelaws were made. The founder member 
Hans Ram Naithani was lifetime Manager 
of the society. After his death, the dispute 
arose. Both of his sons, the petitioner as 
well as the respondent no.3 started 
claiming the position of the Manager in the 
society.
In fact, during the course of 
arguments, it is stated that the wife of the 
respondent no.3 is appointed as Principal 
and she is intervening in the activities of 
the school as are being managed by the 
petitioner Chandra Kishore Naithani.
Before referring the matter to the 
Mediation Centre of this Court, it is 
suggested by the learned counsel for the 
parties, that the parties may be called 
before the Court.
List this matter on 05.07.2023 at 
2:00 PM. Let the petitioner as well as the 
respondent no.3 appear before the Court 
on 05.07.2023 at 2:00 PM after fresh.
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.)
 12.06.2023 Jitendra

WPMS No.1372 of 2023
Hon’ble Ravindra Maithani, J.
Mr. M.C. Pant, Advocate for the 
petitioner.
Mr. T.S. Phartiyal, Additional 
Chief Standing Counsel for the State.
Mr. Ajay Joshi, Advocate 
holding brief of Mr. D.C.S. Rawat, 
Advocate for the Caveator/respondent 
no.2.
Mr. Pankaj Raturi, Advocate for 
respondent no.3.
On the last date, the Court was 
in the process of dictating judgment, 
when possibility was raised that 
perhaps the parties may settle the 
dispute amicably. The dispute has 
been summarized in the Court’s order 
dated 12.06.2023 as follows:-
“It is a dispute with regard to 
the school, which was established 
by the father of the petitioner and 
the respondent no.3 namely, 
Hansram Maithani. He constituted a 
society which was registered. The 
byelaws were made. The founder 
member Hans Ram Naithani was 
lifetime Manager of the society. After 
his death, the dispute arose. Both of 
his sons, the petitioner as well as 
the respondent no.3 started 
claiming the position of the Manager 
in the society.”
On the last date the Court had 
recorded that before referring the 
matter to the Mediation Centre of this 
Court it will be appropriate if the 
parties may be called before the  Court. The petitioner and the 
respondent no.3 are before the Court, 
duly identified by their respective 
counsel. They are brothers.
After interacting with them, this 
Court is of the view that perhaps if
genuine efforts are made they may 
arrive at an amicable settlement and 
that will be better for both of them as 
well as the Institution, for which, they 
are before this Court. Therefore, the 
matter is referred to the Mediation 
Centre of this Court. The parties are 
directed to appear before the 
Medication Centre of this Court today 
itself. 
List on 12.09.2023 along with 
the report of Mediation Centre of this 
Court. 
(Ravindra Maithani, J.)
 05.07.2023
Sanjay

WPMS No.1372 of 2023
Hon’ble Ravindra Maithani, J.
Mr. M.C. Pant, Advocate for the 
petitioner.
Mr. Suyash Pant, Standing 
counsel for respondent no.1.
Mr. D.C.S. Rawat, Advocate for 
respondent no.2.
Mr. Pankaj Raturi, Advocate 
for respondent no.3.
In this petition on 12.06.2023, 
a possibility was explored, as to 
whether the parties may settle the 
dispute amicably? The matter was 
referred to mediation. A report dated 
05.07.2023 from Mediation Centre 
has also been received. According to 
the mediation report, the parties 
have settled the dispute amicably. 
Today, learned counsel 
appearing for the petitioner would 
submit that, in fact, the mediation 
does not resolve anything. A 
resolution has yet to be made. The 
dispute is with regard to the 
position of Manager. Since, the 
mediation report has not been 
accepted though, according to the 
report, it has been signed by the 
petitioner also, the matter shall be 
heard finally. 
List for final hearing on 
11.01.2024.
Learned counsel for the 
petitioner would submit that the  petitioner is being obstructed by the 
respondents from entering in the 
school. 
On behalf of the private 
respondent, it is argued that the 
petitioner is interfering in the 
business of the school. 
The issue before this Court is 
an order passed by an authority, 
which is impugned. If any party has 
any grievance from adverse party, 
he is at liberty to seek such 
recourse, under the law, be it civil or 
criminal, as is permissible. 
(Ravindra Maithani, J.)
 26.09.2023
Sanjay

Children Modern Academy, Dehradun.
